newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline caution limits analyst enthusiasm.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline caution limits analyst enthusiasm.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc's caution over prospects for 1997 is likely to cap enthusiasm over an impressive 1996 performance, analysts said on Tuesday.
The company's full-year results, with pre-tax profit rising 14 percent to 1.545 billion stg, won praise from analysts, with all divisions producing strong or better-than-expected results.
However, there were some reservations over SmithKline Beecham's caution on prospects for earnings growth this year, with the strength of sterling clouding the picture.

Analysts noted that chief executive Jan Leschly played down prospects for double-digit earnings growth in 1997 in the event of the pound staying strong. The company said earlier that current levels of sterling could wipe five percent off 1997 pretax profits.

Leschly told reporters on Tuesday: "We believe (1997) is also going to be a good year. If we exclude the uncertainty that we all have about currency, we can achieve the objective of double-digit earnings in 1997."
One analyst said: "For a company that likes to be bullish, I don't think they were that upbeat."

SocGen analyst Paul Diggle also expressed surprise at the caution, saying there seemed to be enough coming through to keep underlying earnings growth comfortably in the mid teens at constant exchange rates.
But he added that the SmithKline management "have a reputation for being showmen but they don't give hostages to fortune on the numbers."
Although Diggle said some of the higher forecasts for 1997 profits above 1.75 billion stg might edge down, he added that he would not alter his forecast of 1.73 billion stg.

James Culverwell, analyst at Merrill Lynch, said he would also leave his forecast unchanged. "These results came in very much as we expected. There is a very good underlying story and we remain enthusiastic," he added.

Peter Cartwright of Williams de Broe came away with a highly positive view of the management meeting with analysts. He said he would be maintaining hs forecast of 1.68 billion stg, which had already been adjusted for the exchange rate impact.

Cartwright said the group's performance in the fourth quarter at constant exchange rates "was very strong indeed" with sales rising by 18 percent. "The momentum going into the current year is quite racy," he added.

SocGen's Diggle said the customer healthcare business "is performing much more strongly than one would have guessed," boosted by smoking cessation products, the Aquafresh dental care range and the gradual establishment of Tagamet as an over-the- counter product.
Diggle said comment at morning stock broker meetings on Wednesday would be "reasonably positive".

However, he added: "I don't think we will get much in the way of forecast upgrades, if any, so that will mean the shares won't go significantly firmer." Diggle said he was considering whether to raise his neutral stance on the stock to "a qualified buy".

Daiwa analyst Nigel Keegan noted the company's "good, strong" performance relative to the FT-SE 100 index and the pharmaceutical index over the past three years, since former top-selling anti-ulcer drug Tagamet lost its patent.
But he said the stock currently looked "fairly valued" and that he would recommend it as "an add rather than an out-and-out buy". --Jonathan Birt London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
